name: Tubeway Army
label: Beggars Banquet
lede: A London punk trio that couldn't hold on to a drummer found a Minimoog someone had left in the studio, and within a year had the first synth-led No. 1 of the electronic era.

eras.title: Valerian, Scarlett and Rael
eras.text: Gary Webb was a teenage guitarist answering ads in Melody Maker when he walked into a band called the Lasers and met Paul Gardiner. They took on sci-fi stage names, brought in Webb's uncle on drums, and played punk because punk was what got you signed.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paul Gardiner · Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: Gary Webb auditions for the Lasers and meets Paul Gardiner
years.p: Fresh out of Mean Street, Webb tries out as lead guitarist. Bassist Gardiner becomes his closest ally, and when Webb leaves, Gardiner goes with him.

years.cap: Tubeway Army: Gary Numan, Jess Lidyard and Paul Gardiner
years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: Uncle Jess takes the drum stool and the Lasers become Tubeway Army
years.p: Webb's uncle [[Jess Lidyard|b1a5b8e2-a937-4616-93db-dcf2243e4b3a]] joins on drums. Webb renames himself Valerian, Gardiner is Scarlett, Lidyard is Rael.
years.xp:
Valerian probably came from the French sci-fi comic Valérian and Laureline. Webb later admitted the punk sound was a means to an end: he adopted it to get a record deal.

One 1977 show at the Roxy was taped and turned up years later as a bootleg; it's one of only two known live recordings of the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paul Gardiner
years.h: Beggars Banquet signs Tubeway Army
years.p: The independent label takes on the trio in October 1977, four months before their first single.

eras.title: Punk on paper, synths by accident
eras.text: Two singles went nowhere, drummers came and went, and a gig with the Skids ended in a fight. Then a Minimoog in the corner of a studio changed everything, and the label was not pleased.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: "That's Too Bad" is a bid for commercial punk
years.p: Tubeway Army's debut single makes no impact on release. A 1983 reissue reaches No. 97.

years.cap: Gary Numan on guitar with Tubeway Army, 1978
years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: An album's worth of demos for Beggars, shelved until 1984
years.p: The band tapes its songbook so the label can hear what it has. The tapes come out six years later as The Plan.

years.cap: Tubeway Army as a four-piece, on the back of the Bombers single, 1978
years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: Bob Simmonds, Barry Benn, Sean Burke: the line-up won't sit still
years.p: Drummers rotate and a second guitarist comes and goes around the "Bombers" single, which doesn't chart. Numan and Gardiner split with the others over the move away from punk.

years.cap: Flyer for Tubeway Army with the Skids at the White Hart, Acton, 1978
years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: Violence stops the last gig halfway, and Numan quits the stage
years.p: Sharing a bill with Skids, the set is abandoned mid-way. Numan, sick of fights at London pub gigs, makes Tubeway Army a studio-only band.

years.big: "One actually squared up to me in the office."
q: When I turned it on, the sound blew me away.
years.src: The Guardian: How we made · Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: Numan finds a Minimoog in the studio and rewrites the punk songs
years.p: Numan, on how Beggars staff took the electronic turn: they'd signed a blond punk-pop act. The money was spent, so the album came out anyway.
years.xp:
"When I turned it on, the sound blew me away," Numan told the Guardian. He converted the band's guitar songs into what he called electro-punk numbers, on a synth he'd come across by accident during the album sessions.

He was little, he said, but leapt out of his seat too: "we were going to have a fight." With no budget left to re-record, the label released what it had.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: Tubeway Army on blue vinyl, credited to a new name: Gary Numan
years.p: The first pressing of 5,000 sells out without charting. Webb has picked Numan out of the Yellow Pages, from a plumber called Neumann.
years.xp:
Numan wanted to drop the band name and release the album under his own; Beggars Banquet said no. The songs lean on J.G. Ballard and Philip K. Dick, and "Listen to the Sirens" opens with a line lifted from the title of Dick's Flow My Tears, the Policeman Said.

After Replicas broke, the debut finally charted in August 1979 and climbed to No. 14.

years.src: Hi-Fi News
years.h: Five days in Chinatown: Replicas at Gooseberry Sound
years.p: A month after the debut, the trio is in a cheap 16-track studio on Gerrard Street. Numan owns no synths, so he rents a Minimoog and a Polymoog.
years.xp:
Gooseberry was popular with post-punk and reggae acts such as Killing Joke and Creation Rebel. Numan noticed its one keyboard, a Roland, had a hole drilled through it so it could be chained to the wall.

Three more tracks followed in January 1979, with a John Peel session around the same time. The album was finished at Marcus Studios.

eras.title: A robot at No. 1
eras.text: In four months Tubeway Army went from a single that didn't chart to the top of both UK charts, on a five-minute song about a machine. Then Numan dropped the name and kept the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
yt: 'Down in the Park' on The Old Grey Whistle Test
years.h: Replicas comes out on the heels of "Down in the Park"
years.p: Lead single "Down in the Park" misses the chart, then outlives almost everything: [[Marilyn Manson|5dfdca28-9ddc-4853-933c-8bc97d87beec]] covered it, and it's in the film Times Square.

years.big: Two half-songs, a pub piano and one wrong note
years.src: The Guardian: How we made · Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
yt: The story behind the song, Top 2000 a gogo
years.h: "Are 'Friends' Electric?" enters the chart at No. 71
years.p: Numan wrote it on an out-of-tune piano his parents bought. Stuck on two songs, he played one after the other and kept it: over five minutes long.
years.xp:
The main melody is a note sharp because he hit a wrong key and liked it better, then played it on a Polymoog with one finger. The "friends" are machines that look human and supply services door to door; this one, Numan explained, is a prostitute, hence the inverted commas.

Makeup artist Mary Vango styled him for the sleeve with pale skin and heavy kohl, thinking of the candlelit look of Kubrick's Barry Lyndon.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
yt: 'Are Friends Electric' on Top of the Pops, 1979
years.h: Dressed in black and barely moving, the band plays Top of the Pops
years.p: With [[Ultravox|7e786a4c-c743-4713-9340-a6f12d8515d4]]'s Billy Currie, [[Chris Payne|320ba2ed-9892-464a-bbfb-041019837961]] and [[Cedric Sharpley|099a08a2-8d7c-4997-889f-03e7d993cb5d]] added, Numan stands like an android. It was stage fright, he said later.
years.xp:
He had spots that week, Numan said, so the TV crew plastered him in white makeup and blacked his eyes: "My so-called image fell into place an hour before going on the show."

[[Ultravox|7e786a4c-c743-4713-9340-a6f12d8515d4]]'s Systems of Romance was the template; Numan named its song "Slow Motion" as the blueprint for what he wanted.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
yt: 'Are Friends Electric?' on The Old Grey Whistle Test
years.h: The same song, live on The Old Grey Whistle Test
years.p: The BBC2 slot, as much as the chart run, is what grabbed the British public, according to Wikipedia's history of the band.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · The Guardian: Gary Numan comeback
years.h: Four weeks at No. 1, and Replicas tops the album chart too
years.p: The single reaches No. 1 at the end of June. By December it is the fourth best-selling UK single of 1979, and Numan says it sold a million.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army · Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: A Peel session credited to Gary Numan retires the band name
years.p: At the peak, Numan premieres four new songs on John Peel under his own name. Gardiner stays on bass; "Cars" is next.
years.xp: Numan was the band's only songwriter, producer and face, so the name went. The musicians stayed on as his backing band, and the same circle later formed Dramatis after his 1981 farewell shows.

eras.title: Afterlives of a two-album band
eras.text: Tubeway Army never played again, but the records kept turning up: demos, reissues, a Sugababes No. 1. Gary Numan eventually took Replicas back out on the road.

years.src: Wikipedia: Paul Gardiner
years.h: Paul Gardiner dies in Northolt, aged 25
years.p: Gardiner, who had struggled with heroin addiction, died of an overdose of Valium and Diconal combined with cold weather, according to Wikipedia. Numan wrote "A Child with the Ghost" for him.
years.xp:
After Tubeway Army, Gardiner played bass on The Pleasure Principle and Telekon and toured with Numan through 1981. His solo single "Stormtrooper in Drag", sung by Numan, reached No. 49, and his "Venus in Furs" was the first release on Numan's Numa label.

Numan marked the 25th anniversary in 2009 by playing the demo of "Complex" with Gardiner's picture on the screen behind him.

years.src: Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: The 1978 demos finally surface as The Plan
years.p: Beggars Banquet releases the punk-era tapes and they reach No. 29, six years after the band recorded them for the label's ears only.

years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan
years.h: Sugababes go to No. 1 with "Are 'Friends' Electric?" underneath
years.p: "Freak Like Me" mashes Adina Howard's song over the Tubeway Army hit, and the robot is back at the top.

years.cap: Promotional photo for the 2008 Replicas tour
years.src: Wikipedia: Gary Numan · Wikipedia: Tubeway Army
years.h: Numan plays Replicas start to finish, B-sides included
years.p: A sold-out 15-date UK and Ireland tour marks 30 years since the album and Numan's 50th birthday. Replicas Redux follows.
